data.long_meaning: In Persian culture, Mehruz means 'Pearl'. Pearls are symbols of beauty, purity, and rarity. In Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) described pearls as a blessing from Allah. The name Mehruz carries the meaning “Pearl” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mehruz usually hope their child will grow to embody pearl and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Mehruz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pearl.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mehruz total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: مهرز

She is best known for her beauty, intelligence, and her tragic love story with Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni. Mehruz was the daughter of the ruler of Ghazni, Ibrahim Yazdi, and was renowned for her extraordinary beauty. Sultan Mahmud fell deeply in love with her and went to great lengths to win her heart, even proposing to her multiple times. However, Mehruz rejected him due to her deep devotion to her father and her unwillingness to betray him. In frustration, Mahmud attacked and destroyed Ghazni, killing Mehruz's father and brothers. Unable to bear the loss and the guilt of her father's death, Mehruz took her own life.

Her life and teachings have been a source of inspiration for many Sufis and mystics in India and beyond.
